trello.name: Set up Stripe subscription tiers (Basic, Pro, Enterprise) in Stripe
trello.desc:
Create three subscription tiers in Stripe with the following pricing and feature sets:
- Basic: $29/month — basic access to AI model selection tool and limited feature set.
- Pro: $49/month — additional features and priority support.
- Enterprise: $99/month — all features, custom support, and integration options.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Log into the Stripe dashboard.
2. Create products and pricing plans for Basic, Pro, and Enterprise tiers.
3. Configure feature descriptions and metadata as needed.
4. Ensure the tiers are correctly configured and testable.

Acceptance criteria:
- All three tiers exist in Stripe with correct pricing ($29, $49, $99).
- Each tier is active and can be referenced by the app via Stripe API.
- Feature sets are documented and associated with each plan.

trello.name: Build frontend checkout flow using Stripe Elements
trello.desc:
Implement a checkout process using Stripe Elements that is customizable and secure, and matches the app's design.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Integrate Stripe Elements into the frontend.
2. Style the checkout form to match the app’s design (clean and straightforward).
3. Make the checkout button prominent.
4. Implement graceful error handling for invalid card details or insufficient funds.
5. Include a tooltip or help icon explaining what happens if the user chooses a different plan later.

Acceptance criteria:
- Checkout form renders correctly and matches app design.
- Invalid card details and insufficient funds errors are handled gracefully with clear messages.
- A tooltip/help icon explaining plan changes is present.
- Checkout button is prominent and clearly visible.

trello.name: Update pricing page to reflect new subscription tiers
trello.desc:
Update the existing pricing page to display the three new subscription tiers (Basic, Pro, Enterprise) with clear feature comparisons.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Review the current pricing page design.
2. Add sections/cards for Basic ($29), Pro ($49), and Enterprise ($99).
3. Include a clear comparison of features for each tier.
4. Ensure users can easily understand what they get with each plan.

Acceptance criteria:
- Pricing page shows all three tiers with correct pricing.
- Feature comparison is clear and easy to understand.
- Design is clean and straightforward.
- Users can initiate checkout from the pricing page.

trello.name: Build user dashboard for subscription management
trello.desc:
Create a user dashboard that provides real-time subscription management functionality.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Design and implement a dashboard view showing current plan details and billing info.
2. Add options to upgrade, downgrade, or cancel subscription.
3. Provide access to invoices and payment history.
4. Add ability to update payment methods.
5. Ensure the dashboard reflects current subscription status in real-time.
6. Implement notifications for changes such as successful plan upgrades or payment failures.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dashboard displays current plan details and billing info.
- Users can upgrade, downgrade, or cancel their subscription.
- Users can view invoices and payment history.
- Users can update payment methods.
- Subscription status updates in real-time.
- Users receive notifications for subscription changes and payment failures.

trello.name: Integrate Stripe API backend for subscription management
trello.desc:
Implement backend integration with Stripe’s API to handle creating subscriptions, processing payments, and managing subscription lifecycle.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Integrate Stripe API into the backend.
2. Implement subscription creation when a user selects a plan and completes payment.
3. Implement payment processing logic for successful and failed payments.
4. Ensure backend updates user subscription status accordingly.

Acceptance criteria:
- Backend can create subscriptions via Stripe API.
- Successful and failed payments are handled correctly.
- User subscription status is updated based on payment results.
- API endpoints are accessible to the frontend.

trello.name: Set up webhook handlers for Stripe events
trello.desc:
Create webhook handlers for the following Stripe events:
- invoice.payment_succeeded: Confirm successful payments and activate or continue the user’s subscription.
- invoice.payment_failed: Notify users of failed payments, prompt them to update payment information, and consider sending an email notification.
- customer.subscription.deleted: Manage cases where users cancel subscriptions, update access rights, and possibly offer a chance to re-subscribe.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Configure webhook endpoints in Stripe dashboard.
2. Implement handlers for invoice.payment_succeeded, invoice.payment_failed, and customer.subscription.deleted.
3. Ensure handlers update the system correctly for each event.
4. Create test scenarios to simulate different events (payment failures, cancellations, successful payments).
5. Test handlers thoroughly.

Acceptance criteria:
- Webhook endpoints are registered in Stripe.
- All three webhook events are handled correctly.
- invoice.payment_succeeded activates/continues subscription.
- invoice.payment_failed notifies user and prompts payment info update; email notification considered.
- customer.subscription.deleted updates access rights and offers re-subscription option.
- Handlers are tested with simulated events.

trello.name: Integrate frontend with backend subscription API
trello.desc:
Connect the frontend components (checkout, dashboard) with the backend subscription API to ensure real-time updates and seamless user experience.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Wait for backend API and webhook setup to be ready.
2. Connect checkout flow to backend subscription creation endpoint.
3. Connect dashboard to backend endpoints for subscription details, invoices, and payment methods.
4. Ensure any changes to the subscription are reflected in real-time on the dashboard.
5. Handle integration errors and provide clear notifications to users (e.g., payment failure instructions).

Acceptance criteria:
- Frontend successfully communicates with backend API.
- Subscription changes reflect in real-time on the dashboard.
- Errors during integration are handled with clear user notifications.
- Payment failure messages include instructions on how to fix the issue.

trello.name: Implement user notifications for subscription events
trello.desc:
Create frontend notifications for various subscription-related events.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Implement notification UI for subscription confirmations.
2. Implement notification UI for payment errors and failures.
3. Implement notification UI for plan upgrades/downgrades.
4. Ensure notifications are clear and actionable.

Acceptance criteria:
- Users receive notifications for subscription confirmations.
- Users receive clear notifications for payment errors with instructions.
- Users receive notifications for plan changes.
- Notifications are non-intrusive but clearly visible.

trello.name: Prepare detailed test plan for subscription flow
trello.desc:
Create a comprehensive test plan covering manual and automated tests for the entire subscription lifecycle.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Draft a test plan document.
2. Include test scenarios for sign-up, billing, subscription management, payment failures, cancellations, upgrades, and downgrades.
3. Cover both manual and automated test cases.
4. Include edge cases (e.g., invalid cards, insufficient funds, webhook failures).
5. Share the test plan with the team for review.

Acceptance criteria:
- Test plan covers the full subscription flow from sign-up to billing to subscription management.
- Manual and automated test cases are included.
- Edge cases are documented.
- Test plan is shared with Alex and Jordan for review.

trello.name: Create user documentation and help section/FAQ for subscriptions
trello.desc:
Once the subscription feature is live, create clear user-facing documentation and an FAQ/help section.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Draft user instructions on how to manage subscriptions.
2. Draft instructions on how to access invoices.
3. Draft instructions on how to handle common issues (payment failures, plan changes, cancellations).
4. Create a help section or FAQ page covering common subscription questions.
5. Publish documentation in the app or on the website.

Acceptance criteria:
- User documentation covers subscription management, invoices, and common issues.
- FAQ/help section is accessible and covers common subscription questions.
- Documentation is clear and easy to understand.

trello.name: Document API endpoints and webhook event handlers
trello.desc:
Create technical documentation for the backend API endpoints and webhook event handlers to support future maintenance and troubleshooting.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Document all subscription-related API endpoints (request/response formats, parameters).
2. Document webhook event handlers and their behavior.
3. Store documentation in a shared location accessible to the team.
4. Ensure documentation is kept up to date with implementation.

Acceptance criteria:
- All API endpoints are documented with request/response formats.
- Webhook handlers are documented with event types and system updates.
- Documentation is accessible to the team for maintenance and troubleshooting.

trello.name: Schedule follow-up meeting for next week to review progress
trello.desc:
Set up a follow-up meeting next week to review progress on the Stripe integration and address any issues or blockers.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Schedule a meeting invite for next week.
2. Include Alex, Jordan, and Taylor as attendees.
3. Prepare an agenda covering progress on frontend, backend, webhooks, and any blockers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Follow-up meeting is scheduled for next week.
- All team members are invited.
- Agenda includes progress review and blocker discussion.
